summary: Coverage baseline for the daily ingestion workflow. 'observed' is the coverage confirmed when this baseline was accepted; 'floor' is the alarm threshold, set at or below observed to tolerate normal per-source variance. The run fails when coverage drops below a floor (a regression), reports 'degraded' while documented gaps remain open, and asks for the baseline to be raised when coverage rises above observed.

intelligence.reason: Several governed publishers reject automated retrieval (HTTP 403) or expose no authoritative original-page evidence. The floor sits below observed because per-source availability fluctuates daily.

blog.reason: All four governed blog sources publish again: AfDB via a Firecrawl-recovered feed, UNECA via its sitewide feed, and World Bank and ISS via article-page evidence. Floors sit below observed because individual publishers intermittently refuse automated retrieval.

commodity.reason: All five identities now publish a current dated quote: lithium, cobalt, copper, and gold from Trading Economics, and Guinea bauxite FOB from AluHub. Firecrawl can intermittently time out or fail to expose source-specific quote evidence for multiple scraped market pages in the same run, so the floor preserves a usable two-quote minimum while still alarming when coverage falls below it.

countryScore.reason: No trusted country-score release exists. World Bank coverage reaches 43 of 54 countries at the unchanged 0.80 confidence and coverage thresholds; the remaining eleven lack recent tax-revenue and reserves data and need approved secondary institutional sources. Until a complete release publishes, the dashboard serves the static baseline and the live post-write gate stays advisory.
